title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Finance, and the China Disabled Persons' Federation on Issuing the Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities during the Twelfth Five-Year Plan Period
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate
Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Civil Affairs, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Finance, China Disabled Persons' Federation

Circular on Issuing the Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities during the 12th Five-Year Plan Period

CDPF Document No. 28 [2011]

All higher people's courts, people's procuratorates, departments (bureaus, commissions) of justice, public security, civil affairs, human resources and social security, education, health, and finance of all provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the central government, and cities designated with independent planning status; disabled persons' federations; the Disabled Persons' Working Committee of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; and the Disabled Persons' Working Committee of Heilongjiang Provincial Bureau of Agricultural Reclamation:

To ensure the effective implementation of legal aid for persons with disabilities during the 12th Five-Year Plan period, in accordance with the Outline of the 12th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the Cause of Persons with Disabilities in China (2011-2015), the Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities during the 12th Five-Year Plan Period has been formulated. It is hereby issued to you for your earnest execution.

December 29, 2011

(This document is to be forwarded to the county level)

Implementation Plan for Legal Aid for Persons with Disabilities during the 12th Five-Year Plan Period

I. Background

- During the 11th Five-Year Plan period, the state actively promoted judicial fairness and safeguarded social justice and judicial authority. To further strengthen the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Health, and the China Disabled Persons' Federation jointly established a legal aid system for persons with disabilities. Nationwide, 56 legal aid workstations for persons with disabilities were set up. Effective measures were taken to provide legal aid services to persons with disabilities, exploring effective ways to resolve issues of access to justice for disadvantaged groups.

- Courts, procuratorates, judicial administrative organs, public security organs, civil affairs departments, human resources and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations at various levels worked in close coordination to jointly carry out legal aid work for persons with disabilities. They promoted the establishment of local coordination mechanisms for legal aid work for persons with disabilities, leveraged the functions and roles of legal aid workstations for persons with disabilities, and provided safeguards for persons with disabilities to obtain legal services.

- With the rapid economic and social development, cases involving legal and litigation issues concerning persons with disabilities have been increasing. However, the common difficulties faced by persons with disabilities in hiring lawyers and filing lawsuits have not been effectively alleviated. There is an urgent need to address these issues through further in-depth legal aid work for persons with disabilities.

To further improve legal aid work for persons with disabilities, this Plan is formulated in accordance with the Outline of the 12th Five-Year Plan for the Development of the Cause of Persons with Disabilities in China.

II. Task Targets

- A coordination mechanism for legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall be generally established at and above the county level.

- A legal aid system for persons with disabilities shall be established and improved, with judicial aid provided by people's courts and people's procuratorates at all levels, and legal services and legal aid provided by judicial administrative organs at all levels as the primary components, supplemented by legal aid provided by disabled persons' federations at all levels and social forces.

- The construction of legal aid workstations for persons with disabilities shall be accelerated, gradually forming a network of legal aid work for persons with disabilities, and actively providing legal aid services to persons with disabilities.

III. Main Measures

(1) Conduct in-depth legal aid work for persons with disabilities. Courts, procuratorates, judicial administrative organs, public security organs, civil affairs departments, human resources and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations at all levels shall actively incorporate legal aid work for persons with disabilities into their work plans and arrangements, and jointly promote the in-depth development of legal aid work for persons with disabilities nationwide.

(2) Effectively strengthen the construction of coordination mechanisms for legal aid work for persons with disabilities. A coordination mechanism for legal aid work for persons with disabilities, including courts, procuratorates, judicial administrative organs, public security organs, civil affairs departments, human resources and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations, shall be generally established at and above the county level. The normalization and institutionalization of coordination work shall be continuously strengthened, and the mechanism shall effectively play a role in formulating major policies and handling major cases involving the rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

(3) Actively provide judicial aid to persons with disabilities. People's courts at all levels shall reduce or exempt relevant litigation costs for qualified parties with disabilities, simplify the procedures for applying for judicial aid, and gradually expand the scope of judicial aid for persons with disabilities. People's procuratorates at all levels shall actively strengthen the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities and provide corresponding judicial aid services to persons with disabilities in need.

(4) Strive to provide legal aid and legal services to persons with disabilities. Judicial administrative organs at all levels shall continuously expand the fields and content of legal services for persons with disabilities, extending legal services for persons with disabilities to communities, villages, and old revolutionary base areas, areas inhabited by ethnic minorities, border areas, and poverty-stricken areas. According to the different needs of persons with disabilities, timely provision of personalized and professional services shall be made to lawfully resolve their practical interest issues. Legal aid departments at all levels shall regard persons with disabilities as important targets for legal aid; continue to promote the inclusion of matters concerning the protection of the rights and interests of persons with disabilities into the scope of supplementary legal aid matters, ensuring that legal aid cases for persons with disabilities that meet the requirements receive sufficient funding subsidies; and continuously expand the coverage of legal aid for persons with disabilities to benefit more persons with disabilities. Public security organs, civil affairs departments, human resources and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and other relevant departments shall actively take effective measures to provide legal aid services to persons with disabilities and effectively safeguard their rights and interests.

(5) Accelerate the construction of legal aid work institutions for persons with disabilities. At the provincial, municipal, and county levels where conditions permit, courts, procuratorates, judicial administrative organs, public security organs, civil affairs departments, human resources and social security departments, education departments, health departments, and disabled persons' federations shall jointly establish 500 legal aid workstations for persons with disabilities, gradually forming a network of legal aid work for persons with disabilities. The standardization of legal aid workstations for persons with disabilities shall be strengthened, socialized work methods shall be enhanced, and the functions and roles of serving persons with disabilities shall be fully utilized. Through various channels and means, organizational personnel guarantees, capacity and technical guarantees, and financial guarantees for legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall be strengthened.

(6) Encourage and support social groups, non-governmental organizations, institutions of higher learning, etc., to provide legal aid services to persons with disabilities through various forms. Coordination and cooperation between different types of legal aid institutions for persons with disabilities shall be strengthened, and experiences in legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall be promptly summarized and promoted.

(7) Strengthen information management of legal aid work for persons with disabilities, establish a website for legal aid for persons with disabilities, and facilitate persons with disabilities in obtaining legal aid services. Cooperate with relevant institutions of higher learning and scientific research institutes to strengthen basic theoretical research on legal aid work for persons with disabilities, laying a foundation for in-depth development of legal aid work for persons with disabilities. Promote the establishment of a work model for disabled persons' organizations to support litigation and non-litigation, and gradually establish a public interest litigation system for the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities.

IV. Inspection and Evaluation

(1) All localities shall formulate specific development plans based on this Plan and their actual local conditions.

(2) In 2013, a mid-term inspection of legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall be conducted; in 2015, a final inspection and acceptance of legal aid work for persons with disabilities shall be conducted.
